extracted.intended_audience: Researchers conducting systematic reviews, especially those preparing preregistrations on OSF (e.g., pharmaceutical systematic review researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a detailed systematic review protocol to the Open Science Framework (OSF) before conducting the review, specifying key methodological elements to increase transparency, reduce bias, and improve reproducibility. Commonly used in pharmaceutical and clinical evidence synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the research question as part of the preregistered protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preregistration should include the research question up front so the scope and aims of the review are clear before data collection and synthesis begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document the search strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the search strategy in the preregistration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of databases to be searched, search terms/strings, date ranges, and any limits or filters to be applied so the search is reproducible and transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify inclusion and exclusion criteria for study selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state eligibility criteria (population, intervention, comparator, outcomes, study designs, settings, languages, publication types) to prevent post hoc selection decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe data extraction procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify data extraction procedures in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define what data will be extracted, how extraction will be performed (e.g., number of reviewers, use of piloted forms), and how discrepancies will be resolved to promote consistency and reduce errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefine the analysis plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the analysis plan (including synthesis methods) before conducting the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail whether and how meta-analysis will be performed, statistical models, subgroup/sensitivity analyses, and handling of missing data to avoid analytic flexibility and selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preregister protocol before conducting research
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit the detailed plan of the review methodology to OSF before the research is conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preregistration involves committing to a predetermined plan prior to data collection/analysis; doing so reduces the risk of bias introduced during the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote transparency, accountability, and rigour
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize transparency, accountability, and rigour in conducting and reporting the systematic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSF preregistration is presented as a methodology that emphasizes these values so that the review process is clear and trustworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the protocol publicly accessible for scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the preregistered protocol available on OSF for other researchers to access and scrutinize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public accessibility allows others to verify that the study was conducted as planned and helps minimize selective reporting or post hoc changes that could compromise findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to predetermined plan to reduce bias and selective reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: By preregistering, researchers commit to a predetermined plan, reducing risk of bias and selective or post hoc reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment to the protocol minimizes post hoc changes and selective reporting, thereby enhancing the integrity and reliability of the review's conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance reliability and ethical, responsible conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Use preregistration to enhance the reliability of systematic review research and promote responsible and ethical conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page frames OSF preregistration as fostering a culture of openness in scientific inquiry and evidence synthesis, which supports ethical research practices and trustworthy results—particularly relevant to pharmaceutical systematic review research.
